subject: Pilot: Redwood eval onramp — next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@rivermarkhealth.com>, Anne Park <anne.park@rivermarkhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot: Redwood eval onramp — next steps

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps to get the pilot moving. I kept this tight so we can action it quickly.

Call highlights (from Rivermark):
- Primary use: clinical triage assistant in intake flows (structured prompts, short answers, high precision).
- Hard constraints: PII must be removed from test data; responses must flag uncertain/unknown items.
- Success metrics: intent-match >= 92%, hallucination rate < 3% on labeled set, avg latency < 200ms p90 (hosted) or configurable on Dedicated.

Redwood recommendation (shortlist):
- Candidate models for benchmark: Mistral-7B-Instruct (fast, high precision for short prompts), Llama-3-13B-qat (better long-context handling if you expand prompts), and Redwood-compat-7B-v2 (our tuned baseline for fidelity/cost).
- Suggested quantization profile: 4-bit QAT for inference runs to reduce token cost; we can provide predictions on cost per 1k tokens for each model.

Eval plan (proposed):
1) Data: start with a 500-row anonymized sample CSV. Required columns: id, prompt, expected_label, acceptance_notes, metadata.json (optional). See attached rivermark_prompt_set_v1.csv sample.
2) Scoring rubric: (a) intent-match (binary), (b) hallucination flag (binary), (c) safety flag (binary) — we compute weighted score and give per-case annotations. Template: redwood_eval-template.xlsx attached.
3) Execution: Redwood runs the inference and returns raw outputs + scorer labels; we can also return model token-cost breakdown and per-route latency.
4) Timebox: initial runs + scoring for 500 rows typically 3 business days after sample receipt; full 2k sample run ~5 business days.

Security and data handling:
- Please confirm whether you prefer Sandbox in us-west (default) or eu-west; this affects available model variants.
- We can run the pilot on Dedicated sandbox (isolated GPUs) if you prefer to avoid multi-tenant hosted env.

Next steps I propose:
- You produce 500 de-identified rows by EOD Thu (we included an anonymization checklist with pointers).
- We schedule a 30-min kickoff runbook session (I'll invite Ben from Ops) — proposed: Thu 2027-05-06 10:00 PT.
- After receipt, we run the baseline models, share a scoring dashboard, and sync on remediation.

Attachments: rivermark_prompt_set_v1.csv (sample), redwood_eval-template.xlsx (scoring & results format), data-anonymization-checklist.pdf (guidance).

If that plan looks good I’ll send a calendar invite and Ben will provision the sandbox.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com]

From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@rivermarkhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Anne Park <anne.park@rivermarkhealth.com>, Rivermark Eval Team <eval@rivermarkhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot: Redwood eval onramp — next steps

Karthik — thanks for the fast recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Data/PII: We will provide de-identified samples but need a short checklist from you that matches our privacy team’s requirements (what constitutes adequate de-identification for the pilot). Is the checklist you mentioned sufficient for our privacy review?
2) SOC2 / hosting: Can you confirm whether hosted API runs are SOC2 compliant by default or if we must use Dedicated/Private for any sensitive data in the pilot?
3) Costs & timeline: ballpark cost for the 500-row run and whether any additional engineering time is expected on our side.

We’re aligned on the models; our initial focus is precision over recall. If you can just confirm the anonymization checklist and SOC2 posture we’ll start preparing the sample. Also add our CS lead to the kickoff if possible.

—Tom
Tom Lee | Director of Product, Rivermark Health
[tom.lee@rivermarkhealth.com]

Hi Tom — Ben here (Ops). Quick answers to help unblock privacy/security review: 

- SOC2: Redwood’s hosted Redwood API is SOC 2 Type II certified; we can provide the report under NDA. For extra isolation we can run the pilot on a Dedicated sandbox (isolated GPUs + restricted network).
- Anonymization checklist: attached (data-anonymization-checklist.pdf). Key points: strip direct identifiers, hash IDs, remove free-text PHI or mark with [REDACTED], keep schema examples. We can accept pseudo-IDs if you need to re-link during analysis.
- Cost estimate: 500-row baseline run across 3 models (Mistral-7B-Instruct, Redwood-compat-7B-v2, Llama-3-13B-qat) ~ $1,200 — includes runtime + scoring (one-off). If you pick Dedicated sandbox, there’s a small provisioning fee (~$400). We’ll give exact numbers in the HubSpot deal.

I’ll provision a us-west sandbox and share access once we have kickoff time and a user list. If you prefer eu-west please tell us.

Ben Carter | Technical Ops, Redwood Inference
[ben_carter@redwoodinference.com]
